questions.prompt: Match each layer of the URL shortener to the right test level.

pairs.right: Unit test with a fake repository
Integration test with a disposable DB

questions.explanation: Pure logic → unit/property; a service → unit with a fake; a real seam → integration; the critical journey → one E2E.

questions.prompt: Why does the redirect flow get the single end-to-end test?

options.text: It's the cheapest thing to test
It's the critical journey — if it breaks, every link fails
Unit tests can't run in this project

questions.explanation: You reserve scarce E2E tests for the highest-value journey, which here is create-then-redirect.

items.text: Assess risk and plan the test levels
TDD the core logic and unit-test edges
Integration-test the repository, add one E2E
Add coverage/mutation checks and wire up CI

questions.explanation: Plan by risk, build the core test-first, cover the seams and the journey, then add quality checks and CI.

questions.prompt: A `decode(encode(n)) == n` check verified across many generated inputs is a ____-trip property.
questions.explanation: The round-trip (inverse) property is ideal for encoders/decoders and pairs well with Hypothesis.

questions.prompt: Which are sound capstone practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep integration tests hermetic with a disposable database
Inject the id/time source so codes are deterministic
Test the whole app only through 30 browser tests
Spot-check key logic with a mutation run, not just coverage %

questions.explanation: Hermetic integration, injected determinism, and mutation spot-checks are sound; an all-E2E suite is an ice-cream cone.

questions.prompt: A mutation run shows a survivor on encode(). What's the right response?

options.text: Add the assertion or boundary case that distinguishes the mutant, killing it
Add a retry to the test

questions.explanation: A survivor marks a gap in assertions/cases; add the distinguishing test (e.g., a two-char boundary) to kill it and harden the logic.
